question.prompt: Let \[ \begin{aligned} x&=0.123456789101112\\ &\phantom{={}}\ldots998999, \end{aligned} \] where the digits are obtained by writing the integers \(1\) through \(999\) in order. The \(1983\)rd digit to the right of the decimal point is

solutions.explanation:
Group the written integers by their number of digits, because every integer in one group contributes the same amount. The integers \(1\) through \(9\) contribute \(9\) digits. The \(90\) integers from \(10\) through \(99\) contribute \(90\cdot2=180\) digits. Thus there are
\[
9+180=189
\]
digits before the entry \(100\).

The desired position within the three-digit entries is therefore
\[
1983-189=1794=598\cdot3.
\]
Each three-digit entry occupies three consecutive positions, so this exact multiple of \(3\) lands on the final digit of the \(598\)th three-digit integer. Since \(100\) is the first such integer, the \(598\)th is
\[
100+(598-1)=697.
\]
Its final digit is \(7\), choice D.
solutions.title: Count digits in blocks
